messages:
raj: customer reports sudden latency regressions. model calls from their VPC private egress are hitting eu-west endpoints even though their workload has always egressed via us-west NAT. p95 went from ~180ms to 1.2s. they see requests to api.redwood.com resolve to 3.125.45.67 (eu NAT)

maya: can you paste the traceroute + the public egress IP they observe? also did they change any onprem proxy rules or peering in the last 24h?

raj: here are the snippets they pasted (sanitized):

```
$ host api.redwood.com
api.redwood.com has address 3.125.45.67

$ traceroute api.redwood.com
traceroute to api.redwood.com (3.125.45.67), 30 hops max
 1  10.0.0.1 (10.0.0.1)  0.3 ms  0.2 ms  0.2 ms
 3  peering-hub  10.20.1.1  2.0 ms  1.9 ms
 5  eu-egress-proxy.int.example.net (52.16.10.5)  45.1 ms  45.0 ms  44.9 ms
 7  edge-eu.api.redwood.net (3.125.45.67)  46.2 ms  46.0 ms  46.1 ms

$ curl -v -H 'Host: api.redwood.com' https://api.redwood.com/v1/ping
* Connected to 3.125.45.67 (3.125.45.67) port 443
> GET /v1/ping HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.com
> X-Forwarded-For: 198.51.100.22
> X-Client-Region: eu-west-1   # set by their onprem proxy
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```

raj: their observed public egress is 52.16.10.5 (eu NAT) — their onprem proxy seems to be rewriting/keeping a region header and traffic is being hairpinned to the hub which SNATs via the EU pool. they say no intentional config change but they did push a proxy upgrade last night.

sre_jordan: looks like classic hub-peering hairpin + SNAT selection problem. possible causes:
- BGP path changes caused default egress from their hub to prefer a transit that exits through the eu NAT pool.
- Onprem proxy is adding X-Client-Region which our smart-routing picks up and prefers eu model variant.
- Conntrack re-use: existing conntrack entries can cause subsequent flows to reuse an old SNAT IP if upstream NAT pools were rebalanced.

sre_jordan: quick checks to run on their side:
```
# check egress route used for internet
ip route get 8.8.8.8
# dump conntrack for flows to our model IP
sudo conntrack -L | grep 3.125.45.67
# verify proxy no-proxy list for api.redwood.com
# check BGP/peering path changes in last 2 hours (transit provider UI)
```

maya: temporary mitigations while we investigate:
- add a no-proxy entry for api.redwood.com so traffic egresses directly from their local NAT (if appropriate).
- remove/override X-Client-Region/X-Redwood-Region headers at the proxy so our smart-routing doesn't force EU variants.
- if they can't change proxy, we can pin their tenant to us-west model endpoints from our side (short lived) — need eng approval.

raj: I asked them to run the ip route and conntrack commands. they replied: their ip route shows default via peering-hub and conntrack shows many entries translating 10.x -> 52.16.10.5 for flows to 3.125.45.67.

raj: they added a no-proxy for api.redwood.com as a test and re-ran curl: api now resolves to 52.47.88.12 (us-west NAT) and traceroute shows us-west edge. p95 dropped back to ~170ms. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: escalated to eng-oncall @ingrid for follow-up and to record mitigation steps in the tenant's config.

ingrid: good catch. please capture: timestamps, sample conntrack entries, the onprem proxy version they upgraded, and the peering BGP change window. i'll coordinate with network team to prevent cross-region SNAT selection on our routing layer (we may need to adjust regional NAT affinity heuristics).

raj: posted all artifacts to the support ticket and noted mitigation applied. customer happy for now but asked for root cause confirmation.

maya: follow-up actions:
- eng: review smart-routing heuristics that use region headers vs IP geolocation.
- ops: add a runbook entry for 'egress hairpin -> wrong-region' that includes no-proxy quickfix and conntrack flush instructions.
- support: confirm proxy vendor+version and recommend config to avoid adding region header.

raj: will keep the ticket open until eng sign-off. :eyes:
